subject: Office Practice
examFormat: Two papers taken at one sitting. Paper 1 has fifty multiple-choice objective questions, all to be answered within one hour for 50 marks. Paper 2 has a question on a simple case study and six other essay-type questions; candidates answer the case study and any four of the others. The paper carries 100 marks and lasts 2 hours 10 minutes.

topics.name: The Office
objectives: Define the office
State the functions of the office
Describe the layout of the office
Explain the principles of office organization: span of control, unity of control, unity of function, etc.
Describe office procedures
Identify the sections of the office

topics.name: Departments in an Organization
objectives: List the departments in an organization
State the functions of each department in an organization
Draw an organizational chart

topics.name: Office Equipment
objectives: Explain the meaning of office equipment

Identify the types of office equipment: manual (typewriter, perforator, stapling machine, duplicating machine, etc.) and electrical (typewriter, photocopier, shredding machine, computer, scanning machine, facsimile machine, etc.)
State the uses of office equipment
Describe the care of office equipment

topics.name: The Reception
objectives: Explain the meaning of the reception
State the duties of the receptionist
Identify the documents handled by a receptionist
State the qualities of a receptionist
Describe the procedures for handling telephone calls

topics.name: Office Documents
objectives: Explain the meaning of office documents
Identify the types of office documents: administrative, sales, stores and purchasing
State the uses of office documents
Prepare office documents

topics.name: Office Correspondence
objectives: Explain the meaning of office correspondence
Identify the types of office correspondence: memos, business letters, notice of meetings, minutes of meetings, reports and circulars

topics.name: Mail
objectives: Identify the types of mail: personal, official, urgent and confidential
Classify mail as incoming or outgoing
Describe the procedures for handling incoming and outgoing mail

topics.name: Filing
objectives: Define filing
Describe the systems of filing: vertical, lateral and electronic
Describe the classifications of filing: alphabetical, chronological, numerical, geographical, alpha-numerical and subject
State the purposes of filing
State the steps involved in filing
Identify filing equipment

topics.name: Communication
objectives: Define communication
State the importance of communication
Identify the types of communication: verbal (oral, written) and non-verbal (visual, audio, audio-visual)
Identify the methods/media of communication: print (newspapers, magazines, directories, handbills, flyers, etc.) and electronic (radio, television, audio and video conferencing, etc.)
Identify communication service providers: NIPOST, NITEL, media houses, satellite stations, the internet and Global System of Mobile Communication (GSM)

topics.name: Meetings
objectives: Define a meeting
State the purpose of meetings
Identify the types of meeting: statutory, emergency, board, management, Annual General Meeting, staff and committee meetings
Describe the procedure for conducting a meeting

Follow the order of business: opening prayer, agenda, chairman's opening remarks, reading, correction and adoption of the last minutes, matters arising, main business, any other business (AOB), chairman's closing remarks, adjournment/closing and closing prayer
Explain meeting terminologies: agenda, adoption, AOB, adjournment, etc.
State the roles of the chairman/secretary
Write the minutes

topics.name: Report Writing
objectives: Explain the meaning of a report
Identify the types of formal report: short report, long report, investigative report and routine/periodic report
Identify the parts of a report
State the importance of report writing

topics.name: Information
objectives: Define information
Identify the types of information
State the uses of information
Identify the sources of information
Describe the storage of information
State the qualities of good information: timeliness, accuracy, speed of delivery, usability, etc.
